health_zone_table.basis: SitRep77 Tableau 2 (2026-07-30) transcribed and reconciled against the INSP PDF (16 pages, sha256 49eaf5bb4ca1165f2d2f75c3d0afaeda2eaeba56e216970c0d065cf74f180580); all 49 integrated zone rows close exactly to the DRC headline. Wanie-Rukula remains pending harmonization and is not added.

reconciliation.note: The 49 integrated zone rows close to 3605/1587. The delta from reviewed SR74 is +245/+100 across three report days because SR75-76 are not in the reviewed chain. Tableau 1 and 2 report +73 cases and +24 deaths for this day, while prose says +77 cases and the header separately notes seven Haut-Uele deaths integrated through harmonization. Daily flow and multi-day cumulative movement are therefore kept distinct.

lab_indicators_24h.note: Denominator-bearing rows cover Ituri (241 documented / 62 positive) and Nord-Kivu (147 analysed / 15 positive): 77/388 = 19.8%. Haut-Uele reports six positive results but no usable sample denominator; Tshopo has three samples pending. This partial apparent positivity is a testing-process indicator, not a national transmission estimate.

care_continuity: SitRep77 reports 748 patients in isolation (337 confirmed / 411 suspected) at 71.3% national occupancy; Ituri is 523/820 = 63.8%, while Nord-Kivu remains over capacity at 202/141 = 143.3%.

The patient-flow identity does not close: 799 at J-1 plus 118 admissions minus 158 exits equals 759, eleven above the stated 748 end-of-day census. The end-of-day provincial and confirmed/suspected decompositions do close and are promoted with this conflict visible.
The SitRep reports 163 facilities preselected for free essential-care support, but only 43 already receive partner support; official no-fee direction and contracting remain incomplete.
Only 181 of 1170 triage units are reported functional, while frontline burden reaches 151 confirmed infections and at least 44 deaths across the three reporting provinces.
The SitRep explicitly states that continuity of essential health services is compromised, increasing indirect non-Ebola mortality.
highlights: The integrated footprint is 49 of 140 health zones across five provinces. Kabondo is the newly integrated Tshopo zone; Wanie-Rukula is described as a fifth Tshopo zone but remains pending harmonization and is not added to the canonical table.
The DRC headline 3605/1587 closes exactly from 49 detailed zone rows.
Tableaux 1 and 2 report +73 cases in 24 hours, while prose says +77 and contains zone additions that exceed both totals; +73 is promoted from the reconciled table.
National contact follow-up is 75.3% from the Table 4 total 13455/17863; the header and printed Nord-Kivu row are each lower by 35 and are preserved as source conflicts.
North Kivu remains severely over treatment capacity at 202/141 = 143.3%.
Apparent positivity is 19.8% over denominator-bearing Ituri and Nord-Kivu rows only; Haut-Uele lacks a usable denominator and Tshopo results are pending.
Alert investigation is 84.1% nationally, but only 70.04% in Ituri and 33.8% in Tshopo; the printed total-alert row is arithmetically wrong and the component sum is used.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: SitRep77 Tableau 3 components close at 1535 total alerts (70 carried + 1465 new), 1291 investigated and 374 validated suspects. The printed total-alert row says 1135, an arithmetic typo; Sud-Kivu is ND and not coerced to zero.

challenges.finding: Reluctance toward post-mortem sampling, community resistance and insecurity targeting burial teams delay confirmation, under-estimate cases and disrupt response activities.
challenges.response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams and increase burial-team capacity.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of providers and strikes in Bunia and Rwampara interrupt response activities including safe and dignified burials.
challenges.response: Regularise provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: CTE/CT capacity is insufficient: 143.3% occupancy in Nord-Kivu and six Ituri structures above capacity, including Nizi at 322% and Lita at 140%.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up remains weak and declining: Ituri 75.5%, Nord-Kivu 74.7%, Tshopo 66.2% and Haut-Uele 80.6%, with multiple zones at 0% or nonreporting.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays; reinforce supervision and investigate the Ituri decline.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points delay transfer and isolation.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy treatment capacity by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient essential medicines and medical inputs weaken holistic case management.
challenges.response: Urgently procure and distribute essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs and only 181 of 1170 triage units functional raise nosocomial risk; Ituri reports 137 frontline infections/41 deaths, Nord-Kivu 11/3 and Haut-Uele 3 infections.
challenges.response: Urgently procure IPC supplies and reinforce IPC training.

challenges.finding: Extension to Haut-Uele and Tshopo alongside high mobility raises urban, riverine and cross-border spread risk.
challenges.response: Activate priority PoE/PoC and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Proximity laboratories remain insufficient, prolonging confirmation delays and allowing transmission to remain undetected.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across response pillars.
challenges.response: Mobilise resources urgently and advocate with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access linked to CODECO and ADF restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential health services is compromised, raising indirect non-Ebola mortality.
challenges.response: Implement free care effectively and reinforce continuity of essential health services.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: Table 4 total and adjacent prose reconcile at 13455/17863 = 75.3% when Nord-Kivu uses the prose values 4262/5702 = 74.7%. The printed Nord-Kivu row and page-1 header are each lower by 35 (4227/5667 and 13420/17828). Sud-Kivu is closed/NA; missing zones are not zero.

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep77 Tableau 6: 748 end-of-day isolation (337 confirmed / 411 suspected) over 1049 beds = 71.3%. Provincial and case-status decompositions close, but 799 J-1 + 118 admissions - 158 exits = 759, leaving an unexplained 11-patient flow imbalance.

priorities.priority: Relieve North Kivu's 143.3% occupancy immediately; 202 patients are reported against 141 beds.
Restore alert investigation in Ituri and Tshopo, at 70.04% and 33.8% respectively.
Raise national follow-up from 75.3% toward 95% and restore missing Kambala, Mahagi and Rungu reporting.
Restore triage and IPC inputs: only 181/1170 triage units are functional while frontline burden continues to rise.
Repair resistance to sampling and safe burials through trusted local leadership while protecting response teams.
Operationalise no-fee care and partner support for the 163 preselected facilities; only 43 currently report partner support.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep77 national headline is DRC-only (3605 confirmed / 1587 deaths); the country-scope snapshot adds Uganda 20/2/11 separately -> 3625 confirmed / 1589 deaths / 662 recovered.
INCIDENCE CONFLICT: Tableaux 1 and 2 close at +73 cases, while highlights say +77 and listed zone additions exceed both. The reconciled table value +73 is promoted.

TSHOPO ZONE CONFLICT: cover text lists five Tshopo zones including Wanie-Rukula, while Tableaux 1 and 2 integrate four and the narrative says Wanie-Rukula remains pending harmonization. Kabondo enters the canonical 49-zone table; Wanie-Rukula does not.

CONTACT CONFLICT: Table 4 total/prose reconcile at 13455/17863 with Nord-Kivu 4262/5702, while the printed Nord-Kivu row and page-1 header are each lower by 35. The reconciled total/prose values are promoted.
ALERT TOTAL CONFLICT: provincial components and prose yield 1535 total alerts, while the printed total row says 1135. The component sum is promoted.

PATIENT FLOW CONFLICT: 799 at J-1 + 118 admissions - 158 exits = 759, not the stated 748 end-of-day census. The independently closing provincial and confirmed/suspected end-of-day totals are promoted with the 11-patient imbalance visible.
NORD-KIVU CUMULATIVE CONFLICT: highlights prose says 364 confirmed / 254 deaths, while Tableaux 1 and 2 close at 366/242 and the national totals require 366/242. The tables win.
LABORATORY DENOMINATOR LIMIT: Haut-Uele reports six positives without a usable denominator; Tshopo has three pending samples. Apparent positivity is partial, not national.
SOUTH KIVU MISSINGNESS: no provincial report was transmitted; all flow indicators remain ND and are not coerced to zero.

Tableaux 1 and 2 report +73 cases while prose says +77; the reconciled table value is promoted. The delta from reviewed SR74 spans three report days and is not labelled 24-hour incidence.
Contact totals are promoted as 13455/17863 = 75.3% using the total row and adjacent Nord-Kivu prose; the page-1 header and printed Nord-Kivu row are each lower by 35 and retained as conflicts.
The printed alert total 1135 conflicts with the exact provincial/component sum 1535; 1535 is promoted.
End-of-day isolation closes by province and status at 748, but the patient-flow identity yields 759; the 11-patient imbalance is preserved.
